title: Bitcoin AI Model Review — Week 34: 4 of 6 Calls Correct
meta_description: Week 34 graded: 4 of 6 Bitcoin calls correct (67%). All-time: 55.6% over 18 public calls. Paper portfolio +15.3% vs holding.

intro: For week 34 of 2026, covering 2026-08-17 to 2026-08-22, the model delivered 4 hits out of 6 resolved calls, achieving a 66.7 percent weekly accuracy rate.
The week started strong with a four call winning streak before concluding on a 2 call miss streak.
days: On Monday the model called a hold with 59 percent confidence, which was correct as price moved 0.6 percent.
Tuesday brought a correct buy signal at 95.9 percent confidence with a 5.46 percent gain.
Wednesday and Thursday added two more winning buy calls at 87.8 percent and 98.5 percent confidence as Bitcoin surged 10.23 percent and 8.02 percent.
Friday broke the winning run with an incorrect buy call at 98.8 percent confidence when price rose just 0.16 percent.
spotlight: The worst call of the week arrived on Saturday 2026-08-22 when the model issued a buy signal at 98.4 percent confidence.
Bitcoin moved up by just 0.36 percent over the 24 hour horizon, failing to cross the 1.0 percent flat band threshold.
Because the movement remained inside the flat band, this high confidence call was graded as a miss.
It was a clear failure where extreme model certainty was met with stagnant market action.
trend: Bitcoin experienced a sharp mid week rally followed by severe compression going into the weekend.
The signals aligned well with the explosive upward move but failed when volatility vanished into sideways trading.
portfolio: Starting with 10000.0 dollars, the paper portfolio ended at 11533.08 dollars after 19 days and 3 trades, yielding a return of 15.33 percent after paying 43.96 dollars in fees at 0.15 percent per side.
Meanwhile, simple buy and hold produced a return of 19.68 percent to reach 11968.46 dollars.
Following the model signals resulted in a negative 4.35 percent underperformance compared to holding Bitcoin.
record: Across 18 all time resolved calls, the overall model record stands at 10 hits and 8 misses for an accuracy of 55.6 percent.
By signal type, hold calls show 77.8 percent accuracy over 9 calls, buy calls show 42.9 percent over 7 calls, and sell calls show 0.0 percent over 2 calls.
An 18 call sample size is far too small to establish long term certainty, so performance will continue to evolve.

research.title: How the models keep learning without forgetting
paragraphs: The models fine tune on fresh market data around the clock. A replay buffer keeps old training data in the mix, so adapting to this month cannot erase what two years of history taught them.
Any update that scores worse than the current model is rejected outright.
Catastrophic forgetting is the failure that guards against. A model tuned only on the last month becomes an expert on the last month and a novice everywhere else.
